newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest bourse rallies as others close for Easter.
newsitem.headline: Budapest bourse rallies as others close for Easter.

text.p: Hungarian shares continued to gain ground on Thursday and rose three percent in huge turnover as investors apparently lodged their orders before Easter keeps them away from the Budapest bourse, which will trade on Friday.
The BUX index closed at 5,438.97 points, up 157.21.
Spot share turnover surged to 4.80 billion forints from 2.56 billion on Wednesday.
Traders said the rally was still a follow-up of the rally after the Fed's rate hike but they also saw new funds coming to the market.

"Investors' appetite grew, it seems this still stems from the rate hike," said Laszlo Baranyai of Gog Securities. "The other factor is that new market players entered the market bringing fresh funds."
Fears of another rate hike in the U.S. are over for the timebeing but remains a factor, analysts said.

"The question is whether this was a one-off rate hike or was the first step to more hikes," said Rudi Voros of ICE Securities. "This can, of course, negatively influence not only Wall Street, the City but also the Budapest market."
Whatever the case, the Hungarian market still has room to rise, analysts said.

"We think there are still shares in Hungary which are undervalued," Voros said. "We think the Hungarian market trades at around a 20 percent discount to the Czech market according to our 1997 forecasts." He added it was roughly equally valued to the Polish market.

Another analyst, Nigel Rendell, emerging markets strategist at HSBC James Capel in London, suggested that investors should boost Hungary's proportion within their central European portfolio and suggested more focus on domestic oriented firms.
"We believe that investors should overweight the Hungarian equity market relative to the rest of Central Europe," he said in a country report, dated March 26.

On Thursday gas distributor Primagaz was the market's leading gainer with a nearly 15 percent rise of which Peter Nagy of Postabank Securities said earlier today was triggered by lack of supply and some hedging activity.
OTP Bank soared to close at as high as 4,000 forints, up 280, in what an analyst said was in link with Czech bank Komercni Banka 's results.
"Komercni Banka published its figures today and they were very good," said Spencer Jakab, Budapest-based analyst at CS First Boston. "This certainly played a role (in OTP's rally.)"
Komercni and OTP are the only central European banks traded on the SEAQ in London.
Oil company MOL shares closed a fractional 30 forints higher at 3,000 in a huge volume of 541,345 shares.
Traders and analysts said the market may expect a quiet session on Friday with a good number of foreign markets closed.
